solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bulb's leaf blended into rolled cigar

indicators.note: blended into says the leaf letter is mixed in among the other letters
rolled suggests the cigar's letters are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: L is an abbreviation for leaf, as in leaves of a book

explanation.surface: A tobacco leaf is mixed into a hand-rolled cigar, and someone calls it a bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled' turns CIGAR into GARIC; 'blended into' puts L inside it. The 's of 'Bulb's' reads as 'is', linking the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of this pungent kitchen staple grows underground as a bulb made of cloves.

clue.text: A tyre finally evaluated and pumped up

indicators.note: finally says only the last letter of tyre is used

parts.note: rated means assessed or evaluated

explanation.surface: A tyre was checked and then inflated.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerated means filled with air, as something pumped up is.

clue.text: Pasta and fish one consumed in Oxford, say

parts.note: ling is a fish of the cod family

indicators.note: consumed in means swallowed up inside the other word

parts.note: Oxford is an example of a university, uni for short
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Pasta and fish eaten by a student in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguini is a type of flat ribbon pasta.

clue.text: Do less badly in meat factory where all the workers are unionists

definitions.text: factory where all the workers are unionists

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters go inside the meat word

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of do less are put wrongly into a new order

explanation.surface: Doing less poorly in a meatpacking plant whose staff are all union members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges DO LESS into LOSEDS. 'meat factory' reads as one phrase, but 'meat' is wordplay and 'factory' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed shop is a workplace where union membership is compulsory for employees.

clue.text: Junk is put back together?

definitions.meaning: junk is rubbish or waste material
the question mark flags the pun

explanation.surface: Scrap that has been reassembled might be called junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is household rubbish, and re-fuse means to fuse again, a punning second reading.

clue.text: Think highly of members of choir at eisteddfod

indicators.note: members of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being impressed by singers in a Welsh choir at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: An eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of music and poetry. 'of' is a link here; 'Think highly of' is the full sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is to esteem them, to think highly of them.

clue.text: Tell a story connected with research material's components

parts.note: to fib is to tell a small lie, a story
res is a common abbreviation for research

explanation.surface: Lying about research into what a material is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibres are the threads that make up a textile or material.

clue.text: Curse small business drive

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Co is short for company, a business
urge means drive or impulse

explanation.surface: Damning the push for small firms.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is an affliction or bane, something cursed upon people.

clue.text: Records by judge accepted by unqualified farm worker

indicators.note: accepted by means the other letters are taken inside

parts.note: sheer means absolute, unqualified
EPs are extended-play records
to hear a case is to judge it in court

explanation.surface: Records by a judge taken on by an untrained farmhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unqualified' looks like lacking credentials but means SHEER, utter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep shearer is a farm hand who clips fleeces.

clue.text: Solicitor, occupied by one call, is becoming weary

indicators.note: occupied by means the solicitor word has other letters living inside it

parts.note: a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor in a loose sense
I is the Roman numeral one
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A lawyer, interrupted by a phone call, is getting tired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a lawyer but is a TOUT, one who solicits business.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiring out describes someone gradually running out of energy and growing fatigued.

clue.text: Male savage implicated in nurse's death

indicators.note: implicated in means drawn inside another word

parts.note: to tend is to nurse
he is the male pronoun
bitter can mean fierce or savage, as a bitter wind

explanation.surface: A violent man is suspected of involvement in a nurse's death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'death' needs 'the bitter end' in its sense of the very end; the 's of 'nurse's' adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The bitter end is the very last extremity, often death itself.

clue.text: Hospital giving backing to footwear stall

indicators.note: giving backing to means the hospital letter stands behind the footwear word

parts.note: a boot is an item of footwear
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital supports a stall selling shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A booth is a small stall at a fair or market, a synonym.

clue.text: Part-time actor, ignoring a drunken dude, is forced out

indicators.note: ignoring says the letter a is left out of the actor word

parts.note: an extra is a casual actor hired for crowd scenes

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters of dude stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A bit-part player who pays no attention to a drunk man is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops A from EXTRA to leave EXTR; 'drunken' makes UDED from DUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrude something is to push or squeeze it out, as metal through a die.

clue.text: Order as excluded from contract?

indicators.note: excluded from means the letters of as are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: to contract is to decrease, grow smaller

explanation.surface: An instruction that 'as' is to be left out of a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a legal document but is the verb meaning shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order issued by a ruler or court.

clue.text: Film makers arrived before racer smashed front of Williams

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: smashed suggests the racer is wrecked into a new order of letters
front of says only the first letter of Williams is used

explanation.surface: A driver crashes at the start of the Williams team car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' turns RACER into RACRE; Williams is a Formula One team, but only its W is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera crew is the team that shoots a film.

clue.text: Asian one is adopted by another?

indicators.note: adopted by means taken into the family of another word, placed inside it

parts.note: an Indian is another Asian person
one's is a contraction of one is

explanation.surface: An Asian person is taken in by a family from elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a whole as a picture of the answer: an Asian person taken in by another Asian nation's name. 'one is' contracts to one's.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Indonesia, in Southeast Asia, is an Asian by nationality.

clue.text: Thoroughly examines old soldiers

definitions.meaning: to vet is to check carefully

explanation.definitionFit: Vets as a verb means checks closely; as a noun it is short for veterans.

clue.text: Vehicle, one given away, disappeared from sight

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral one
shed means cast off, given away

explanation.surface: A van, one of a pair, gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanished means went out of view entirely.

clue.text: Facade, removed from shop, came apart

indicators.note: the facade of a word is its front letter, here taken off the shop word

parts.note: a store is a shop

explanation.surface: A shopfront has been taken off and the building fell to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facade' is the front letter S of STORE, which is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tore, past tense of tear, means ripped or split apart.

clue.text: Long-distance travellers run over nettles

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the run letter sits above the nettles word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
to nettle is to anger, so nettles means angers

explanation.surface: Someone runs across a patch of stinging plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nettles' looks like plants but is a verb, annoys.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers are wanderers who roam over long distances.

clue.text: Foreign exchange of great size, say

parts.note: forex is the standard short form of foreign exchange
ample means large or plentiful

explanation.surface: A big currency deal, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Say is used to introduce an instance, exactly like the phrase meaning e.g.

clue.text: One who draws a line connected to a boat

definitions.meaning: an artist who draws or paints pictures

definitions.text: a line connected to a boat
definitions.meaning: a rope at the bow used to tie up a small boat

explanation.definitionFit: A painter is an artist, and also the mooring rope at a dinghy's bow.

clue.text: Rose was mentioned in conversation

definitions.meaning: a topic that arose in talk

explanation.definitionFit: Came up means ascended, and also arose as a topic in talk.

clue.text: Absconder losing sight of a take-off point

indicators.note: losing sight of means the letter a goes missing from the word

parts.note: a runaway is someone who has fled

explanation.surface: A fugitive loses track of a place to escape from.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft take off from a long strip of tarmac at an airport.

clue.text: Peacemaker allowing one inside enclosure of racehorse

indicators.note: inside enclosure of means letters are enclosed within the horse word

parts.note: a pacer is a horse bred for harness racing
if can mean provided that, allowing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A peacemaker lets someone into the paddock of a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allowing' looks like a verb of permission but supplies the conditional word if; a pacer is a harness-racing horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacifier brings calm and peace, so is a peacemaker.

clue.text: Dispute raising of outstanding fine

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: raising of in a down clue means the word is turned to read upwards

parts.note: due means owed, outstanding

explanation.surface: Disagreement over hiking an unpaid penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising of' makes EUD from DUE, placed under F.
explanation.definitionFit: A feud is a long-running quarrel or dispute.

clue.text: Ecstasy found in possession of attractive family member

indicators.note: found in possession of means the letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: nice means pleasant or attractive
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug is found on an attractive relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a relative within the family.

clue.text: Sensor that's contaminated by river fungus

parts.note: the ear senses sound

indicators.note: contaminated suggests the letters of that's are polluted into disorder

explanation.surface: A detector that has been polluted by river water.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthstar is a fungus whose outer skin splits into a star shape.

clue.text: Slater, for instance, is first to open school

indicators.note: first to says only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: Someone is first to open a school.
explanation.walkthrough: A slater is a woodlouse, a small crustacean; 'Slater' looks like a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodlouse, called a slater in places, belongs to the crustacean order of isopods.

clue.text: Was stuck with returning red hip boots

indicators.note: stuck with means one word has another stuck into it
returning means the word red is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone was stuck wearing tall red boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns RED into DER. Hip boots are thigh-high waterproof boots worn by anglers.
explanation.definitionFit: Waders are waterproof boots reaching the hip, worn by anglers.
